title: Post-Market Clinical Follow-up Study to evaluate the clinical safety and performance of the 5C® CR knee system
summary:
The clinical follow-up of a medical device after it has been placed on the market, known as a Post-Market Clinical Follow-Up (PMCF) study, is an integral part of the Post-Market Surveillance (PMS) activities for medical devices. Post-market surveillance provides manufacturers with information on whether their medical device remains safe and effective even years after market introduction. It may help identify previously unknown product-related issues and provides insights into changes in the market as well as in user practices and behavior. Ultimately, a robust PMCF program contributes to the development and availability of improved medical devices with reduced risks.
As part of this study, patients will be evaluated at regular intervals following surgery. All examinations conducted before surgery and outside the scheduled study visits are routine clinical assessments performed as part of standard medical care.
Demographic data, such as age, sex, height, weight, and the medical history of the underlying condition, will be collected. During the study visits, the mobility and functional performance of the operated joint will be assessed and documented. This includes a physical examination by the physician to evaluate the range of motion of the operated knee joint, as well as documentation of the patient's assessment of pain and mobility.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent has been obtained from the patient prior to participation in the follow-up study and after appropriate information has been provided.
- The patient undergoes surgery at a participating study site.
- The 5C® CR Knee System manufactured by implantcast GmbH is implanted.
- The patient is skeletally mature.
- The collateral ligaments of the knee to be operated on provide sufficient stability of the knee joint.
- Implantation is performed in accordance with the approved indications:
-- Non-inflammatory degenerative joint diseases, including osteoarthritis and avascular necrosis
-- Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
-- Rheumatoid arthritis
-- Revision surgery (tibial component)
-The patient is willing to participate in follow-up assessments, including telephone interviews and/or on-site evaluations at the clinic.
Exclusion criteria:
- Absence of written informed consent from the patient.
- The patient has an active malignancy at the time of follow-up assessment (i.e., has not been tumor-free for the past 5 years).
- Morbid obesity (BMI ≥ 40 kg/m²).
- Patient age > 99 years at study enrollment.
- The patient is pregnant at the time of informed consent prior to the planned surgery (prospective enrollment).
- The patient is a minor, legally incapacitated, or has limited legal capacity.
- There is evidence that the patient is unlikely to comply with the study protocol (e.g., lack of willingness to cooperate, cognitive impairment).
- Presence of substance abuse or dependency disorders (e.g., alcohol or drug addiction).
- Participation in another clinical trial within 4 weeks prior to study enrollment.
- Presence of an active infection.
- Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the implant materials.
- Physiological or anatomical conditions that preclude adequate bony support of the implant, are unlikely to maintain such support, or do not permit implantation of an appropriately sized prosthesis.
- Untreated vascular disease affecting the involved extremity.
- Metabolic disorders that may impair bone formation.
- Severe axial malalignment and deformities that may compromise implant fixation, accurate positioning, or implant function.
- Ligament instability.
- Severe neuromuscular disorders that significantly impair the affected extremity.
